items.statement: Algebra I
Course Focus
items.notes: [Apply the following to each content standard.]

items.statement: Identify the principles of SDA Christian values in correlation with mathematics.
Recognize God as Creator and Sustainer of an ordered universe.
Value God’s inspired writings and created works as a revelation of His precision, accuracy, and exactness.
Develop accountability as expressed in God’s word and laws.
Employ Christian principles as a basis for learning and growth.
Broaden intellectual abilities through the study of mathematics.
Make biblically-based choices when dealing with mathematical data.
Apply biblical principles of Christian morality, integrity, and ethical behavior to mathematical processes.
Course Abilities
items.notes: [Apply the following to each content standard.]

items.statement: Develop abilities in mathematics.
Understand mathematical concepts (number sense, algebraic and geometric thinking, measurement, data analysis, and probability). MP.7
Utilize the problem-solving process (explore, plan, solve, verify). MP.1, MP.2
Develop higher-order thinking skills (analyze, evaluate, reason, classify, predict, generalize, solve, decide, relate, interpret, simplify, model, synthesize).MP.2, MP.3, MP.4
Attend to precision. MP.6
Be able to apply mathematical knowledge and skills to a variety of purposes.
Use a variety of strategies in the problem-solving process (i.e. patterns, tables, diagrams). MP.7, MP.8
Conduct research (locate, observe/gather, analyze, conclude).
Perform calculations with and without technology in life situations. MP.5
Read critically and communicate proficiently with mathematical vocabulary.
Course Content
items.notes: [Understand, represent, apply, analyze.]

items.statement: Be able to understand concepts involving real numbers.
Simplify expressions using the order of operations, including properties of exponents, square roots, and absolute value.
Identify numbers (i.e. real, rational, irrational).
Identify relationships and operations among numbers (i.e. properties, equations, inequalities, ratios, proportions, dimensional analysis, real vs. imaginary). N-RN.3, A-REI.1
Be able to represent mathematical situations using algebraic symbols and models.
Use and evaluate expressions involving variables. A-SSE.1
Write equations, systems of equations, and inequalities from written and oral expression, recognizing equivalent forms. A-SSE.2, A-CED.1,2, F-LE.2,3, G-GPE.5
Identify, graph, solve, and interpret linear/quadratic equations/inequalities and the concept of variation. A-SSE.3, A-CED.2,
Recognize, evaluate, and interpret functions, including domain and range. F-IF.1,2,4,5,6
Apply basic concepts of statistics and probability (i.e. measures of central tendency, plots, combinations, permutations)
Be able to apply appropriate techniques, tools, and formulas to interpret and solve problems.
Calculate measurable attributes of figures (degrees of angles, lengths, perimeter, area, volume). N-Q.1,2,3
Demonstrate mathematical proficiency using technology when appropriate.
Use and manipulate given formulas to solve a variety of problems (i.e. slope, distance, area, volume, perimeter, midpoint)
Perform operations involving polynomials and rational expressions. A-APR.1,7
Solve consumer-related problems (i.e. profit/loss, sales tax, mark-up/discount, interest) N-Q.1,2,3
Solve simple equations and inequalities in one variable (linear, quadratic, rational, radical, exponential, absolute value).
Solve systems of equations and inequalities using graphs and algebraic methods. A-CED.1, A-REI.1,5,6
Be able to analyze results and draw appropriate conclusions.
Find and interpret information from graphs, charts, and numerical data. S-ID.6,7
Predict patterns and generalize trends (i.e. arithmetic/geometric sequences, scatter plots, linear regressions). F-LE.1
Judge meaning, utility, and reasonableness of findings in a variety of situations, including those carried out by technology.

Course Content
items.notes: [Understand, represent, apply, analyze.]

items.statement: Be able to understand concepts of differentiation and integration.
Understand limits of functions (i.e. definition, graphs, calculating, properties, behaviors, finite, infinite, one-sided).
Identify continuity of functions (i.e. intuitively, definition in terms of limits, and graphically).
Demonstrate knowledge of the derivative (i.e. concept, definition, at a point, as a function, applications, linearization and second derivatives).
Demonstrate knowledge of the integral (i.e. concept, definition of anti-derivatives, techniques, fundamental theorems of calculus, and numerical approximations).
Be able to represent mathematical relationships and situations using calculus.
Interpret applications of the derivative in various situations (i.e. optimization, velocity, speed, acceleration, increasing/decreasing, concave up/down and points of inflection.
Solve a variety of situations (physical, biological, or economic) and represent their limits as definite integrals.
Identify, graph, and interpret various derivatives and integrals in applied contexts.
Present solutions resulting from applications of derivatives and integrals in conjunction with substitution techniques in finding anti-derivatives.
Be able to apply appropriate techniques, tools, and formulas to interpret and solve problems,
Compute the derivatives of functions using the sum, product, quotient, and chain rules.

Use the integral in specific applications to give accumulated change, find the area of a region, the volume of a solid with known cross sections, the average value of a function, and the distance traveled by a particle along a line.
Demonstrate mathematical mastery of a graphing utility.
Be able to analyze results and draw appropriate conclusions.
Find and interpret information from graphs, charts, and numerical data.
Predict patterns and generalize trends.
Judge meaning, utility, and reasonableness of findings in a variety of situations, including those carried out by technology.

items.notes: [Understand, represent, apply, analyze.]

items.statement: Be able to understand concepts of personal finance and business mathematics.
Identify various aspects of stewardship (i.e. costs/benefits, needs/wants, tithes and offerings).
Demonstrate knowledge of the time-value of money and basic financial management.
Be able to represent mathematical situations in personal and business life using graphs, tables, and charts.
Be able to apply appropriate techniques, tools, and formulas to interpret and solve problems.
Demonstrate proficiency in basic math skills used by consumers (i.e. decimals, fractions, percentages, proportions).
Exhibit money management skills (i.e. budgets, checking and savings accounts, risk management, debt management, investments, mortgages, income taxes, and deductions).
Solve consumer-related problems involving time value of money (i.e. simple and compound interest, inflation, present and future values of sums).
Use both mental estimation and technology to make optimal consumer choices.
Be able to analyze results and draw appropriate conclusions.
Find and interpret information from graphs, charts, and financial statements.
Predict patterns and generalize trends.
Judge meaning, utility, and reasonableness of findings in a variety of situations, including those carried out by technology.

items.statement: Be able to understand terms and symbols of geometry.
Demonstrate understanding of undefined terms (point, line, plane, and space). G-CO.1
Interpret properties and relationships among figures using inductive and deductive reasoning.
Understand how basic mathematical systems are built (observations, hypotheses/conjectures, postulates, theorems, corollaries).
Classify and characterize figures and objects (i.e. angles, polygons, polyhedrons, circles, and spheres). G-CO.1, G-C.2,
Recognize various types of symmetry and transformations. G-CO.2,3,4
Be able to represent geometric properties and relationships.
Specify spatial relationships using coordinate geometry. G-CO.5,6
Identify measurable attributes of figures and objects. G-GMD.4
Verify similarity and congruence of geometric figures. G-CO.6,7,8, G-SRT.1,2,3, G-C.1
Be able to apply appropriate techniques, tools, and formulas to interpret and solve problems.
Apply coordinate geometry and algebraic formulas to verify characteristics of geometric figures. G-SRT.5, G-GPE.1,4,5,7,
Select and use an appropriate direct or indirect method of measurement. G-GPE.6, G-C.3,4
Construct geometric figures and objects. G-CO.12,13, G-C.3,4
Use trigonometric functions and laws to solve triangles and find areas. G-SRT.6,7,8,9
Apply geometric methods to solve real-life problems. G-MG.1,2,3
Use formulas to find measurable attributes of figures and objects (i.e. arc, sector, perimeter, area, surface area, volume).
Be able to analyze results and draw appropriate conclusions.
Investigate, apply, and prove properties and theorems. G-CO.9,10,11, G-SRT.4,5, G-C.1, G-GPE.4,5
Find and interpret information from graphs, charts, and numerical data.
Make conjectures regarding meaning, utility, and reasonableness of findings in a variety of situations, including those carried out by technology.
